describes: The settings of single tools: the thresholds, minimum samples and scope of the coverage and mutation gate and the files it mutates as Commands (`threshold*`, `mutationCommands`; the header of `scripts/check-thresholds.mjs`); how long HEAD must sit still in a worktree before `scripts/prune-worktree-branches.mjs` removes it, on every host, unless a caller names it with `--finished` or its branch with `--discard`, how many merged pull requests that sweep reads from GitHub and how long it waits for them (`worktreeGc*`); how much of a failing job's output the git hook runner, `scripts/git-hooks.mjs`, prints (`gitHooksFailedOutputBytes`); the longest one call of `scripts/fresh-run.mjs` may take (`freshRunDeadlineSeconds`); the model `scripts/code-graph.mjs` extracts the documents and names the communities with when it builds the local code graph, with the graphify release the `pypi:graphifyy` pin in `mise.toml` names, the file types whose items it stamps as semantic, the folder it builds into, the name it registers the MCP server under, and the file beside the graph that the harness assessment writes the combined graph to and that the server is registered on while it is current, with the field in it that records the graph it was built from (`graphify*`); how the co-change map of `tools/coupling/coupling.ts` reads the trunk's merged pull requests: the committer address of a merge, the paths it ignores, its rename similarity, the most files a counted pull request may change, and the thresholds of an edge, a rate's sample, a hub and a cluster (`coupling*`); the platforms the toolchain's lockfile, `mise.lock`, covers (`toolchainLockPlatforms`); and the model every TypeSafe question is sent to and the thresholds, skip list, passage sizes, width, cap and offline share of `mise run citations:support` (`typesafeModel`, `citationSupport*`). It holds, too, the threshold of `mise run prompts:incidents` and the fewest words of a paragraph it judges (`promptIncident*`), which reads `typesafeModel` as well; and the agents' GitHub App, its installation, the one repository a token `scripts/github-app-token.mjs` mints may reach and the account that owns it, which the dev container clones, how much of a kept token's hour must be left for it to hand the token out again, and the App's bot account the dev container commits as (`githubApp*`). And it holds the Langfuse projects `scripts/prompt-run-figures.mjs` reads a pending run's figures from, with the environment variables of their keys, the endpoint and field groups it asks for, its page size, the names it counts turns and tool calls by, the usage keys each token figure sums and the one Langfuse adds as their sum, how far back a window opens, and how long and how often it waits on the API (`langfuse*`).
whyThisFileExists: Each of these belongs to one tool, unlike the rest of the policy, and a constant a tool reads still lives in a policy file under a key, with its reason beside it (`CLAUDE.md` § Three kinds of file, and never a fourth). They share one record under `tools/policy/` rather than one beside each tool, so every tunable of the workflow is in one directory (`docs/decisions.md` § D-27). The harness keeps its own record beside it, `tools/harness/harness.config.json`, for the reason `docs/decisions.md` § D-26 gives: its constants are what changes when it is pointed at another harness. That record names six keys here it reads, `couplingMinSampleUnits`, `couplingClusterMinJaccardPermille`, `graphifySemanticExtensions`, `graphifyOutDir`, `graphifyCombinedGraphFile` and `graphifyCombinedGraphBlobField`, and copies none.
gatedBy: mise run check:policy holds this record's header, a `Means` beside every constant, and no key another record also defines. mise run thresholds:check and mise run thresholds:commands:check hold `thresholdPercents`, `thresholdMinSamples`, `thresholdScope` and `mutationCommands`: they refuse any of the four missing, of the wrong shape or with no `Means` sibling, and judge the branch's changed code by their values; mise run thresholds:selftest runs each refusal on a fixture repository carrying a copy of the policy, sized from its minimum samples, and one with the keys removed. mise run worktree:selftest holds `worktreeGcMinAgeHours`: with the liveness check working, a worktree between an agent's calls, and one whose branch's pull request has merged, are kept by the key's reason while HEAD there has been still less than it, one still past it is removed, and one its caller names with `--finished`, or whose branch it names with `--discard`, is removed at once; with the liveness check forced off and the key unreadable, an idle worktree is kept. mise run worktree:selftest holds `worktreeGcMergedPrLimit` as the limit a stub `gh` is asked for; no gate holds `worktreeGcGhTimeoutSeconds`, which bounds a call to GitHub that no gate makes. mise run hooks:selftest holds `gitHooksFailedOutputBytes`: it refuses a policy without the key or its `Means` sibling, and asserts that a failing job's printed output stops at the key's value while a file holds all of it; the runner refuses to start a commit or a push without it. No gate holds the value of `freshRunDeadlineSeconds`: `scripts/fresh-run.mjs` refuses a run without it, and mise run tests:fresh:selftest runs its deadline case through the caller's own deadline instead. mise run citations:support:selftest holds `typesafeModel` and the eight `citationSupport*` keys: it refuses a run whose policy lacks one, or one of their `Means` siblings, or whose threshold or offline share is over 1, and holds both thresholds as inclusive, the skip list, the passage sizes, the cap and the offline fallback a missing key runs; `citations:support` itself reads a token and the network and no gate runs it. `mise run code-graph` reads the six `graphify*` keys, and graphify's release from the `pypi:graphifyy` pin in `mise.toml`, and no job runs it, since it reads the network, a language model and the person's own plan. mise run code-graph:selftest, at pre-push and in CI, runs it against stub tools with the policy's values: it fails on a policy missing any of the six, and holds the `mise.toml` pin as the release the script requires, `graphifyClaudeCliModel` as the model passed to extraction and naming, `graphifyOutDir` as the folder graphify is told to write, `graphifyMcpServerName` as the name registered, and `graphifyCombinedGraphFile` as the file registered when its `graphifyCombinedGraphBlobField` records the graph beside it. mise run harness:selftest holds `graphifyCombinedGraphFile` as the file `tools/harness/graph.py` writes, beside the graph it combines, and `graphifyCombinedGraphBlobField` as the field it records that graph's blob id under, from a fixture record whose field is not this one. No gate holds `graphifySemanticExtensions` to graphify's own list of file types, which lives outside this repository. mise run coupling:check holds the eight `coupling*` keys and reads `prReviewMergeMethod` of `tools/policy/pr-review.json`: it refuses a key missing, without its `Means` sibling or of the wrong shape, and a merge method other than `rebase`, and re-derives the co-change map by their values; mise run coupling:selftest runs each refusal on a fixture repository carrying a copy of the policy with those keys set to the fixture's own, and holds that the live values have the shapes the check reads. mise run harness:selftest reads the six keys `tools/harness/harness.config.json` names from fixture records of its own. mise run check:toolchain holds `mise.lock` to `toolchainLockPlatforms`, refusing a tool with no URL and checksum for one of them, and refuses a policy without the key; mise run check:toolchain:selftest runs that refusal on a copy of the policy given a platform the lock does not cover. mise run prompts:incidents:selftest holds `typesafeModel` and the two `promptIncident*` keys: it refuses a run whose policy lacks one or its `Means` sibling, whose threshold is over 1, or whose fewest words is not a whole number of at least 1, and holds the threshold as inclusive and the fewest words as the least a paragraph sent holds; `prompts:incidents` itself reads a token and the network and no gate runs it. mise run github-app-token:selftest holds the seven `githubApp*` keys. It runs `.devcontainer/entrypoint.sh`'s `clone`, which reads `githubAppRepositoryOwner` and `githubAppTokenRepository` for the clone it makes at a container's first start, against a local repository at the address they give, and refuses with its reason a policy without the owner. It also refuses a policy without `githubAppId` or `githubAppTokenRepository`, or with a `githubAppTokenRefreshSeconds` of 0, by its reason; it holds the identity `identity` prints as made, in GitHub's noreply form, from `githubAppBotLogin` and `githubAppBotUserId`, whatever their values, and refuses a policy without either; it holds the JSON Web Token as signed for the App `githubAppId` names, and the request as made for the installation `githubAppInstallationId` names and for `githubAppTokenRepository` alone, before a stub of GitHub's endpoint; and it holds a kept token with less than `githubAppTokenRefreshSeconds` left as replaced. No gate holds the App's two ids to GitHub, which only a token minted from the App's key can read, nor the bot account's login and id, which GitHub's users endpoint gives, nor the owner to the repository's: the high-risk floor holds all five, through `githubApp*` in `prReviewHighRiskJsonKeys`, to a person. mise run prompt-runs:figures:selftest holds the thirteen `langfuse*` keys: it runs `scripts/prompt-run-figures.mjs` against a stub of Langfuse's API on loopback with the live values but `langfuseBaseUrl`, pointed at the stub, and `langfusePageLimit`, set to 2 or to 3; it holds the field groups as the ones every request asks for, the projects' variables as the keys each is read with, the turn name, the tool-name prefix, the usage buckets and Langfuse's total key as the figures it works by hand, over rows of its own and over the rows of the second read in asdlc-openspec-ic9h.10, the lookback as the start of a window with no earlier analysis, and the retry limit, the longest wait and the timeout as the failures each gives; and it refuses a policy without `langfuseProjects`, field groups naming `io` or without `usage`, a base URL over http to a host that is not loopback or with a path, an observations path of `//host` or `/\host`, a usage key in two buckets, the total key in a bucket, and two projects naming one variable. No gate holds `langfuseBaseUrl`, the projects or the plugin's names to Langfuse itself, which only a live read sees, in the probe dispatch of asdlc-openspec-ic9h.11; the high-risk floor holds the `langfuse*` keys to a person.
whatItDoesNOTDo: It computes nothing: `scripts/check-thresholds.mjs` measures the coverage and the mutation score, and what each of those counts is defined once, in count-index.md § Rates and metrics. It holds none of the harness's own settings, which are `tools/harness/harness.config.json`'s. It holds no setting more than one stage of the workflow reads, which is `tools/policy/vocabulary.json`'s or `tools/policy/agent-workflows.json`'s. It holds no tool's version: each, graphify's among them, is a pin in `mise.toml` (`docs/decisions.md` § D-31 and § D-35).
provenance: Split out of `tools/policy.json` on 2026-10-02 by D-27 (asdlc-openspec-umg3), each key with its value and its `Means` as that file held them at 962358c (`git show 962358c:tools/policy.json`), except that `typesafeModelMeans` now says the helper takes the model from its caller. `thresholdPercents`, `thresholdMinSamples`, `thresholdScope` and `mutationCommands` came with D-13 (asdlc-openspec-j09.10) on 2026-09-28: the thresholds from the strategy's text, and the samples and the split of Commands from Routines as the maintainer chose them from the spike asdlc-openspec-j09.2. `graphifyClaudeCliModel`, `graphifySemanticExtensions`, `graphifyOutDir` and `graphifyMcpServerName` came with D-20 (asdlc-openspec-rsc) on 2026-10-01, beside a key for graphify's release, which D-35 (asdlc-openspec-8juz.3) retired on 2026-10-04 for the `pypi:graphifyy` pin in `mise.toml`. The eight `coupling*` keys came with D-24 (asdlc-openspec-3oln) on 2026-10-02, each value chosen from the measurements of the history through f862fe0 that its `Means` gives. `graphifyCombinedGraphFile` and `graphifyCombinedGraphBlobField` came with D-28 (asdlc-openspec-fot7) the same day. `toolchainLockPlatforms` came with D-31 (asdlc-openspec-8juz.2) on 2026-10-03. Each key carries its date and its evidence in its `Means`. `promptIncidentMinProbability` and `promptIncidentMinWords` came with asdlc-openspec-6yt.5 on 2026-10-05, the first from the experiment in its notes and the second from the paragraphs the prompts gave that day. `githubAppId` and `githubAppInstallationId` came with asdlc-openspec-owva.4 on 2026-10-06, as asdlc-openspec-owva.2 recorded them from the App's settings page the day before, and `githubAppTokenRefreshSeconds` with them, from the token's hour as GitHub documents it, and `githubAppTokenRepository`, from the branch's adversarial review. `githubAppBotLogin` and `githubAppBotUserId` came with asdlc-openspec-irvc the same day, read from GitHub's users endpoint. The first twelve `langfuse*` keys came with asdlc-openspec-ic9h.4 on 2026-10-09: the endpoint, its field groups, paging and limits from Langfuse's OpenAPI spec, docs and source and the first read recorded in asdlc-openspec-ic9h.10, the turn name, the tool-name prefix and the usage keys from the plugin's hooks/langfuse_hook.py at v1.2.1, and the projects' variables named for the secrets asdlc-openspec-ic9h.9 creates. `langfuseUsageTotalKey` came with it on 2026-10-10, from the second read recorded in asdlc-openspec-ic9h.10.
thresholdPercentsMeans: The thresholds `mise run thresholds:check` and `mise run thresholds:commands:check` hold the code a branch changes under apps/ to, each a whole percentage: `lines`, of its changed code lines, those Node's own coverage counts run; `branches`, of the branches Node reports on those lines, those taken; `mutation`, of the mutants StrykerJS makes over the changed code of the Routines and, in a run of their own, of the Commands, those detected. What each counts, who counts it and the value that would mean the project is not viable are count-index.md § Rates and metrics. docs/test-strategy.md § Thresholds gives them as supplied, at least 80% on changed Commands and Routines and at least 90% line and branch coverage, and docs/decisions.md § D-13, items 8 and 9, measures them over the lines a branch changes against origin/main. Each is judged only over its minimum sample, `thresholdMinSamples`. Raising one refuses a change the gate passed before; lowering one passes weaker tests. Where it loses: a change whose every line is run and every mutant detected by tests that each check one thing passes at 100%, and only the honesty lens, reading the tests, sees how little they check. The calculator's first measurement is in the header of scripts/check-thresholds.mjs. Decided 2026-09-28 (asdlc-openspec-j09.10), from the strategy D-13 adopted.
thresholdMinSamplesMeans: The sample below which `scripts/check-thresholds.mjs` gives no rate: `lines`, changed code lines; `branches`, changed branches; `mutants`, the mutants of changed code one mutation run makes, leaving out one a comment ignores and one whose test run errored. Below it the gate prints the counts and refuses each one uncovered, untaken or undetected that no directive excuses with a reason (count-index.md § Rates and metrics; docs/decisions.md § D-13, item 9). They are choices, not measurements: the calculator's past changes measured by the spike asdlc-openspec-j09.2 were either comment-only or at least 50 mutants, 35 code lines and 16 branches, so its data cannot place a floor between. At 20 mutants one is 5 points and 80% tolerates 4 undetected, where the largest net change the spike saw between two runs was 3; at 20 code lines 90% tolerates 2 missed; at 10 branches one is 10 points and 90% tolerates 1. The maintainer chose them on 2026-09-28 (asdlc-openspec-j09.2's notes, answer 4). Raising one sends more changes to the count rule, which refuses any single gap; lowering one lets a rate over a handful pass or fail on one line. Where it loses: a change with 15 mutants and 3 undetected fails, where as a rate it would pass at exactly 80%. Decided 2026-09-28 (asdlc-openspec-j09.10).
thresholdScopeMeans: What `scripts/check-thresholds.mjs` counts as the product's code: `code`, the globs of the files whose lines and mutants it measures, and `tests`, the globs of the files it leaves out, every test file and any helper beside one; a file both match is a test's. Each is a glob under apps/, relative to the repository's root, and they are also Node's coverage include and exclude globs. Only JavaScript is listed, since V8 records the coverage of JavaScript and StrykerJS mutates it here; an app's HTML and CSS are not measured. What counts as changed is the header's: the lines `git diff -U0` gives against the merge base with origin/main, and a file git does not track yet, whole (docs/decisions.md § D-13, item 8). Only changed source lines are mutated, so a change to a file `tests` matches mutates nothing: the maintainer's choice of 2026-09-29 (asdlc-openspec-j09.10's notes), which leaves a weakened test to the test-inventory gate (asdlc-openspec-j09.9). Adding an extension brings its files into both metrics; widening `tests` takes files out of both. Where it loses: a test helper kept outside an app's test/ directory is measured as the product's code, and a script inline in an HTML page is not measured at all. Decided 2026-09-28 (asdlc-openspec-j09.10).
mutationCommandsMeans: The Commands: each key a file under apps/ whose code the tests reach by spawning a process, each value the test files its mutation run runs. `mise run thresholds:commands:check` mutates a Command with StrykerJS's command runner, one mutant at a time, which sees what a spawned process runs. Every other file `thresholdScope` counts as code is a Routine, which `mise run thresholds:check` mutates with the tap runner over every test file no Command lists, so no test that spawns a server is run by the tap runner, which leaves such a server running when it ends a failing test's process (the header of scripts/check-thresholds.mjs has the measurements). A Command's run is a CI step and a change-verify run and not a pre-push job, for its cost, 181-186 s wall for all 72 of serve.js's mutants, a change to every line of it, on the host that header names: the maintainer's choice of 2026-09-28 (asdlc-openspec-j09.2's notes, answer 3), an exception to the gate ladder that docs/decisions.md § D-04 records in its amendment of 2026-09-29. Adding a Command moves its mutants from pre-push to CI; a spawned file left out is scored by the tap runner, which cannot see what the spawned process runs, as 25 of serve.js's 72 mutants were not seen. Where it loses: serve.js's exported functions, which its tests also call in-process, wait for CI with the rest of the file. Decided 2026-09-28 (asdlc-openspec-j09.10).
worktreeGcMinAgeHoursMeans: The hours HEAD must have sat still in a clean worktree whose branch is contained in the trunk, with no process in it, before `scripts/prune-worktree-branches.mjs` (`mise run worktree:gc`, also run by the `WorktreeRemove` hook) removes it, on every host; the script's header says how HEAD's last move is read. A worktree its caller names with `--finished`, or whose branch it names with `--discard`, is removed without waiting. It is 24 because a lane's run is measured in hours and a freshly cut worktree is clean and contained from its first second, so anything shorter can remove a live lane (asdlc-openspec-zlz). It holds where a liveness check works too, since `lsof` or `/proc` sees a working agent only while one of its commands runs, and an agent between two calls has no process in its worktree (asdlc-openspec-m4m). Raising it keeps an abandoned checkout, and its branch, on disk longer; lowering it lets the sweep remove a lane that has not yet committed. Where it loses: a session that works more than 24 hours in one worktree without a commit, checkout or rebase, and with no command running there when a sweep runs, is removed under it, where a longer threshold would have kept it; and a finished worktree no caller names stays until HEAD there has been still 24 hours, where the sweep once removed it at once. Decided 2026-09-29 (asdlc-openspec-zlz), for hosts with no liveness check; read on every host from 2026-10-03 (asdlc-openspec-m4m).
worktreeGcMergedPrLimitMeans: How many of the trunk branch's merged pull requests, newest first, `scripts/prune-worktree-branches.mjs` asks `gh pr list` for, once per sweep, to prove a branch contained when its tip is one's head: a rebase merge gives the trunk new SHAs, and a neighbouring line changed on the trunk gives the replayed commits new patch-ids, so GitHub's record is the one proof that survives both (asdlc-openspec-dxf). The repository had 72 merged pull requests when this was set; 500 lists them all for a while yet, in one call that took 0.71 s. Raising it lengthens the call; lowering it leaves a branch whose pull request is older than the last one listed to the patch-id proofs. Where it loses: past 500 merged pull requests, a branch merged before the newest 500 whose patches changed as they landed is kept, where a larger limit would have proved it. Decided 2026-09-29 (asdlc-openspec-dxf).
worktreeGcGhTimeoutSecondsMeans: The most seconds `scripts/prune-worktree-branches.mjs` waits for its one `gh pr list` call before it reads no merged pull requests and falls through to the patch-id proofs. The `WorktreeRemove` hook runs the sweep synchronously on every teardown, so a host with no network, where a connection can hang rather than fail, would otherwise stall each teardown for as long as `gh` waits. The call took 0.71 s online on 2026-09-29. Raising it lets a slow network still answer, at that cost to an offline teardown; lowering it drops the proof on a slow one. Where it loses: on a network slower than 10 s, a branch whose patches changed as they landed is kept, where a longer wait would have proved it. Decided 2026-09-29 (asdlc-openspec-dxf).
gitHooksFailedOutputBytesMeans: The most bytes of a failing job's output that the hook runner, `scripts/git-hooks.mjs`, prints at a commit, a push or `mise run gates`: the last ones, where a failure's summary is, followed by the path of a file under the temporary directory that holds all of it. A passing job prints one line. Without it one failing job can print past what an agent's tool output holds, which lefthook did (`asdlc-openspec-pp6`, hazard 4): on 2026-10-01 its run with one failing job printed 110,244 bytes, and the harness cut it mid-run. Sized from that day's passing run (`asdlc-openspec-uc1`, step 0d): the largest job printed 23,593 bytes (workflows-selftest), the next two 9,590 and 9,331, and the other 29 under 7 KB each, so three failures print about 25 KB. Raising it shows more of a large failure in one read; lowering it fits more failures in one. Where it loses: workflows-selftest failing on an early case, whose FAIL line sits more than 8 KB before its end, needs a second read of the file, where no cap would have shown it at once. Decided 2026-10-01 by the maintainer, D3 of asdlc-openspec-uc1, from a recommendation put with that case.
freshRunDeadlineSecondsMeans: The most seconds one call of `scripts/fresh-run.mjs` may take, its fresh run or a `--rerun`, from setting its deadline to its last child: a child still running when it passes is killed with every process it started, the clone is removed and the run is refused, saying so. It sits below 600 s, the longest a session's Bash call may wait, so a call the session gives that timeout (the script's header names it) ends by this deadline and its cleanup rather than by the harness killing it with the clone left behind. The Commands' mutation run took 181-186 s over every line of serve.js (the header of scripts/check-thresholds.mjs), inside it with room for the install and the tests. Raising it past 600 s lets the harness kill a call before its own cleanup runs; lowering it refuses a run whose Commands' mutants take longer. Where it loses: a change that touches many Commands at once can take longer than this, and is refused where a longer deadline would have measured it. Decided 2026-09-29 (asdlc-openspec-j09.14, from its pre-PR review).
toolchainLockPlatformsMeans: The platforms `mise.lock` covers for every tool `mise.toml` pins (`docs/decisions.md` § D-31): `mise run check:toolchain` refuses a tool whose lock entry lacks a URL and a checksum for any of them, and the lockfile is written by `mise lock --platform` with exactly this list, comma-separated. linux-x64 is CI's runner and the dev container on an Intel host, linux-arm64 the dev container on Apple silicon, macos-arm64 and macos-x64 a Mac, and windows-x64 native Windows; `mise install --locked`, which CI runs, installs only what the lock covers. Dropping one leaves a machine of that kind to install outside the lock, unverified, or to fail a locked install; adding one needs `mise lock` again before the gate passes. Where it loses: windows-arm64 and the musl builds are not here, so such a machine installs with no checksum from the lock, and nothing here has been run on one. Decided 2026-10-03 (asdlc-openspec-8juz.2), from the platforms the dev container, CI, the maintainer's Mac and README.md § Setup name.
graphifyClaudeCliModelMeans: The model graphify's `claude-cli` backend extracts the documents with when `scripts/code-graph.mjs` builds. The script passes it as `GRAPHIFY_CLAUDE_CLI_MODEL`, the one setting that backend reads for extraction, and `claude -p --model` takes an alias or a full model name. The script also passes it to `graphify cluster-only` as `--model`, so the communities are named with the same model. It is `opus` because the graph the maintainer judged worth having, with its links between documents and code, came from Opus agents, and nothing has measured what a smaller model would miss. Lowering it to `sonnet` or `haiku` spends less of each person's plan per document. Where it loses: a first build sends every document, so each engineer's first build spends Opus on all of them, where a smaller model would cost less. What the script's first build costs is not yet measured (asdlc-openspec-3rx); the agent skill's first build, on the same documents with Opus, cost $10.40 at Langfuse's prices (`docs/decisions.md` § D-20). Decided 2026-10-01 by the maintainer (asdlc-openspec-rsc).
graphifyOutDirMeans: The folder under the primary checkout that `scripts/code-graph.mjs` builds the local code graph into. The script passes it to graphify as `GRAPHIFY_OUT`. `.gitignore` ignores it, unanchored. The `code-graph` skill cites this key; the READMEs, `docs/decisions.md` § D-20 and the script's header spell its value, and no gate holds them to it, so a rename edits each of them in the same change, D-20 by an amendment. It is graphify's own default, so a person running graphify by hand finds the same folder. Where it loses: a rename that misses `.gitignore` would let a person commit the graph, which `docs/decisions.md` § D-20 rules out. Decided 2026-10-01 (asdlc-openspec-rsc).
graphifyMcpServerNameMeans: The name `scripts/code-graph.mjs` registers graphify's MCP server under at Claude Code's local scope, which makes its tools `mcp__<this>__<tool>`. The `code-graph` skill cites this key; the worktree briefing's carve-out, the READMEs and `docs/decisions.md` § D-20 spell its value, and no gate holds them to it, so a rename edits each of them in the same change, D-20 by an amendment, and each person runs `mise run code-graph:mcp` again. Where it loses: a person who already registered another server under this name at local scope has it replaced. Decided 2026-10-01 (asdlc-openspec-rsc).
graphifyCombinedGraphFileMeans: The file, beside `graph.json` in the folder `graphifyOutDir` names, that `tools/harness/graph.py` (`mise run harness:graph`), run from the checkout that holds the graph, writes the combined graph to: the local graph with the harness's wiring and the co-change edges added, recording the git blob id of the `graph.json` it was built from. `scripts/code-graph.mjs` registers the MCP server on it while that id is the `graph.json` beside it, and on `graph.json` otherwise (`docs/decisions.md` § D-28). The harness's config names this key and spells no value. It is neither `graph.json`, which graphify writes, nor `graph-with-wiring.json`, which the untracked script the harness replaced wrote into the same folder on a maintainer's machine, so neither is overwritten. Where it loses: a rename leaves the old file behind, which nothing reads, and the server on `graph.json` until `harness:graph` runs again. Decided 2026-10-02 (asdlc-openspec-fot7).
graphifyCombinedGraphBlobFieldMeans: The field, under the combined graph's `graph`, in which `tools/harness/graph.py` records the git blob id of the `graph.json` it combined, and which `scripts/code-graph.mjs` compares with the blob id of the `graph.json` beside the file before it serves it (`docs/decisions.md` § D-28). Both scripts read it here, through `tools/harness/harness.config.json` for the graph half, so neither spells it: renamed on one side alone, the server would stay on `graph.json`, saying the combined graph records no graph it was built from, with both selftests passing. Where it loses: a rename leaves every combined graph written before it unserved until `harness:graph` runs again. Decided 2026-10-02 (asdlc-openspec-fot7).
graphifySemanticExtensionsMeans: The file extensions whose graph items `scripts/code-graph.mjs` stamps `_origin: "semantic"` after each build that changed the graph, with the items of the node types graphify's parser never makes and every edge that touches one. They are graphify 0.9.73's document, paper, image and office types (lines 48 to 51 of its `detect.py`), every type it sends to the LLM rather than parsing. The stamp stops `graphify update`, if anyone runs it, from deleting those items as parser output (the script's header). Re-derive the list from that file whenever the `pypi:graphifyy` pin in `mise.toml` moves. Adding an extension graphify parses as code would mark parser output as semantic, which `update` then never refreshes; leaving one out lets `update` erode that type's items. Where it loses: a type graphify adds in a later release goes unstamped until this list is re-derived. Decided 2026-10-01 (asdlc-openspec-rsc).
couplingMergeCommitterPatternMeans: The committer address, as a regular expression over the whole of it, of a commit GitHub wrote when it rebase-merged a pull request into `main`: a person's or a bot's `<id>+<login>@users.noreply.github.com`. `tools/coupling/coupling.ts` reads a run of consecutive first-parent commits with one such address and one committer time as one pull request, and any other commit as a direct push, which is no unit of the co-change map. Measured 2026-10-02 through f862fe0: it groups the trunk into 93 runs, and the other 18 commits, made with a local address, are direct pushes. The same day GitHub's own list of the pull requests merged to `main` agreed with the runs one for one, each run ending at a pull request's merge commit; the pull request that carries asdlc-openspec-3oln gives that check, which reads the network and is not re-derived here. Where it loses: a direct push made with a noreply address reads as a pull request, and a merger whose merges carry another address reads as direct pushes, which shows as `directCommits` rising in the diff when the baseline moves. An exact list of addresses would lose instead the first merge by a new account. Decided 2026-10-02 (asdlc-openspec-3oln).
couplingIgnoredPathsMeans: Globs, as Node's `path.matchesGlob` reads them, of the paths whose changes the co-change map of `tools/coupling/coupling.ts` leaves out, counted as `ignoredChanges`. `artifacts/coupling/**` is the map itself: each move of its baseline would otherwise couple it to whatever that pull request also changed. Measured 2026-10-02 through f862fe0: `ignoredChanges` is 0, since no pull request had yet touched the map, and the first move of the baseline after this one will ignore one. Adding a glob removes its paths from `files`, `edges` and `clusters`, so a lane check reading the map knows nothing of them. Where it loses: a generated file that does move with its inputs, such as `artifacts/trace/record.json` with the specs and tests it is read from, stays in and ranks as coupled to them, which it is, though no person edits it. Decided 2026-10-02 (asdlc-openspec-3oln).
couplingRenameMinSimilarityPercentMeans: The similarity, in whole percent, at or above which the co-change map reads a path deleted and a path added in one pull request as a rename (`git diff-tree -M<this>%`), so the file's earlier changes follow it to its new name; below it the old name's changes are dropped, since that file is gone. 50 is git's own default, so `git log -M` agrees with the map. Measured 2026-10-02 through f862fe0: 40, 50 and 60 give the same map, 74 dropped changes, 128 files and 847 edges with no cap, so no rename in the history so far sits near the line. Where it loses: a move that also rewrites more than half of the file starts its history again at the new name. Decided 2026-10-02 (asdlc-openspec-3oln).
couplingMaxUnitFilesMeans: The most files a merged pull request may change and still be counted by the co-change map; one that changes more is an `oversizedUnit`, left out of every count, because a sweep couples every pair of files it touches whether or not they belong together. Files are counted as named at the baseline, after dropped and ignored ones. Measured 2026-10-02 through f862fe0 over the 93 merged pull requests: median 4 files, 90th percentile 17, largest 35, 30, 29, 26 and 26. The 35 is #56, a fan-out sweep of sixteen unrelated ready issues; the 30 archives one change into the living spec, and the 29 is #99, which moved every git hook to this repository's own runner, each one piece of work. 30 leaves out #56 alone, with 90 pull requests counted and two empty: 730 edges at `couplingMinTogether`, against 847 with no cap. 25 would leave out five, #99 among them, and 206 edges with them. Where it loses: a later sweep of 30 files or fewer is counted, and couples its unrelated issues' files. Decided 2026-10-02 (asdlc-openspec-3oln).
couplingMinTogetherMeans: The fewest counted pull requests that must change two files together for the pair to be an edge of the co-change map. 2 is the smallest count that is a recurrence, the count `promptReviewRecurrenceCount` holds a finding to. Measured 2026-10-02 through f862fe0 with `couplingMaxUnitFiles` at 30: 730 edges at 2, 378 at 3. Raising it keeps only stronger pairs; 1 adds every pair any pull request ever touched together. Where it loses: two files changed together once, in the only pull request either has had, are no edge, so a lane check reading the map sees them as unrelated. Decided 2026-10-02 (asdlc-openspec-3oln).
couplingMinSampleUnitsMeans: The sample under which the co-change map writes no rate (`CLAUDE.md` § Reporting honesty): an edge's `jaccardPermille` is null when fewer than this many counted pull requests changed either of its files, and every `hub` and the `clusters` are null when fewer than this many pull requests are counted. What the two rates count is count-index.md § Rates and metrics. It is a choice, made from its measured effect: through f862fe0 on 2026-10-02, 3 of the 730 edges have no index at 3, 30 at 5, 70 at 8 and 101 at 10. At 5, one pull request is a fifth of the smallest denominator an index is written over. Raising it leaves more edges without an index, and so out of every cluster. Where it loses: two files changed together in each of the four pull requests that touched either are as close a pair as there is, and get no index. Decided 2026-10-02 (asdlc-openspec-3oln).
couplingHubMinPercentMeans: The share of counted pull requests, in whole percent, at or above which the co-change map marks a file a hub: changed with nearly everything, as a registry every new script or rule adds a row to is. A hub keeps its `files` row and its edges and is left out of `clusters`, which would otherwise join around it into one. Measured 2026-10-02 through f862fe0 over 90 counted pull requests: the most-changed files' shares fall 50, 39, 33, 27, 27, 22, 22, 21, 20, 20, 18 and 17%, then 13%, the largest gap below the top. 15% cuts there, and its twelve hubs are README.md, tools/policy.json, git-hooks.yml, the bead skill, scripts/README.md, docs/decisions.md, package.json, .github/workflows/verify.yml, CLAUDE.md, tools/README.md, docs/playbook.md and .claude/README.md. At 20% the last two are not hubs, and .claude/README.md forms a cluster with scripts/workflows.selftest.mjs; at 25% five are hubs, and with `couplingClusterMinJaccardPermille` at 300 one cluster holds 39 files. Where it loses: which files a hub moves with, such as the scripts CLAUDE.md changes with, is in no cluster, though its edges say it. Decided 2026-10-02 (asdlc-openspec-3oln).
couplingClusterMinJaccardPermilleMeans: The Jaccard index, in thousandths, at or above which an edge between two non-hub files joins them in one cluster of the co-change map; a cluster is a connected group of such edges, and a person reads it as a seam a decomposition could keep whole. Measured 2026-10-02 through f862fe0 with `couplingHubMinPercent` at 15: at 300 the largest cluster holds 18 files, the calculator's tests and the trace and test-strategy gates joined through package-lock.json and the worktree briefing; at 400 it holds 11, the trace and test-strategy gates alone, and each of the eight clusters reads as one concern: the change-* skills, the pull-request reviewer, the dev container, the calculator's tests, the trace gates, OpenSpec's checker, the in-session guard and the citations gate; at 500 the largest holds 3. 400 is the lowest whose every cluster reads as one concern. Lowering it merges concerns; raising it splits them into pairs. Where it loses: two files that always change together, but each often alone as well, fall under it and stay out of one cluster. Decided 2026-10-02 (asdlc-openspec-3oln). Since 2026-10-04 (D-37, asdlc-openspec-qcqm) `partnersOf` reads it too: a file paired with a changed one at or above it, which the change leaves alone, is printed in the branch reviewer's brief as evidence, which decides nothing. The pull-request reviewer's verdict printed it too until 2026-10-05 (D-46, asdlc-openspec-m8hs).
typesafeModelMeans: The model every TypeSafe question in this repository is sent to, read here by each tool that asks one and passed to `tools/lib/typesafe.ts`, which reads no policy itself. Pinned and not `jev-latest`, so a run can be reproduced and a probability means the same on the day it is read as on the day its threshold was set: a threshold is calibrated to one model, and the 2026-09-29 experiments behind the first caller (`asdlc-openspec-6yt`) ran on this one. It is changed here only, by a person who has re-measured every caller's threshold on the new model. Where it loses: the service retires a pinned model one day, and every caller then fails with the SDK's error until this key is edited, where `jev-latest` would have gone on answering with a model no threshold was measured on.
citationSupportMinProbabilityMeans: The probability of `supports` under which `mise run citations:support` prints a citation as not supported: the citation is read against this, and a citation at or above it is silent. Measured over the 437 citations the command judged in this repository on 2026-09-30, before this change's own files were added to it, with `jev-1.13.0` (the `--min` flag re-runs it): 68 fell under 0.5, 21 under 0.3 and 3 under 0.1, and a re-run moved the count at 0.5 by a few (65 to 68). It is 0.3 because a list of 68 is not one a person reads to the end, where 21 include the one defect a reading confirmed, the `bd` row of `docs/playbook.md` § 1. Words you will meet (line 53 that day) citing `README.md` § Setup for a sentence that sits in the file table at README.md:93, under 0.15 in both runs. The note on `asdlc-openspec-6yt.2` proposed 0.5 with 2 of 120 real citations flagged there; that figure did not reproduce over the whole repository, and the count here is the one this key is set from. Raising it toward 1 prints more citations and more noise; lowering it toward 0 prints only the surest ones and misses a borderline pointer. Where it loses: a sentence that points at a section for where a step lives and not for what it says (`Decided by: <file> § 3`) scores low however well cited, and most of the 21 are of that shape.
citationSupportSkipPathsMeans: Files, or path prefixes, whose citations `mise run citations:support` does not judge, so a person is not sent to read what cannot be edited. The register is the one, its frozen file and, since 2026-10-08 (asdlc-openspec-vjgj), the records under its directory: an entry is never rewritten, a later decision adds a dated amendment (`CLAUDE.md` § Decisions live in the register), so an entry that cites what a document said before an amendment is correct history and reads as contradicted to a judge given the document as it is now. It is a file's path, exactly or as a prefix, and the files under a `HISTORY` root in `tools/citations/scan.ts` are skipped without being listed here. Where it loses: a citation written wrongly in the register goes unjudged; `citations:check` still checks that it resolves.
citationSupportSectionMaxCharsMeans: The most characters of a cited passage `mise run citations:support` sends TypeSafe with a citation: a section whole up to it, and a cut, marked in the report, beyond. Set at the 32,000 that the note on `asdlc-openspec-6yt.2` gives as the state budget; the SDK and API pages read for that task state no limit, and a request the service refused would fail the run and not be skipped. The section is sent whole because the 2026-09-29 experiment's fixed passage carried up to 6,000 characters and separated real citations from swapped ones at an AUC of 0.959, and a claim about the rest of a section cannot be judged from its start. Raising it costs input tokens on every long section; lowering it cuts a passage before the sentence a citation is about. Where it loses: a section of a prompt file with no headings after its label runs to the end of the file, and is cut where the sentence cited may lie past the cut.
citationSupportClaimLineMaxCharsMeans: The most characters of each of the three lines round a pointer that `mise run citations:support` sends as the claim: a longer line is cut to a window of this width round the pointer, so the pointer is never cut off. It exists for the table row and the JSON string that hold a whole paragraph on one line: on 2026-09-30 this file had 41 lines over 800 characters, the longest 7,476, and a pointer on such a line would otherwise send it whole as a claim and dwarf the sentence about the pointer. 800 is the width the first version used; it was not measured against a range of widths. The three-line claim itself was measured against the pointer line alone (see `citationSupportMinProbabilityMeans`). Raising it sends more of a long row, and more of the neighbours a pointer's sentence does not concern; lowering it cuts a long sentence's own words away from its pointer. Where it loses: a table row holding several pointers is windowed round the first one named on it, so the other pointers on that row are judged against text that may not carry their own sentence.
citationSupportLineContextMeans: How many lines either side of a cited line or range `mise run citations:support` sends as the passage for a `file.md:NN` citation, which names a line and not a section. Three carries the sentence a line belongs to in this repository's wrapped prose without taking in a neighbouring section. Raising it takes in the next paragraph and the judge can then be satisfied by a passage the citation did not point at; lowering it to none judges one wrapped fragment of a sentence. Where it loses: a table row cited by line is judged against its neighbouring rows, which can support a claim about the row above it.
citationSupportConcurrencyMeans: How many TypeSafe requests `mise run citations:support` has in flight at once. Sixteen is enough to judge the whole repository in seconds, and the bound keeps a rate limit (the SDK retries a 429) from being met at five hundred requests at once, which the 2026-09-29 experiment's unbounded fan-out never tested. Raising it shortens a whole-repository run and raises the chance of a 429; lowering it to 1 sends one at a time. Where it loses: nothing but wall time, since a failed call fails the run at any width.
citationSupportMaxCitationsMeans: The most citations one run of `mise run citations:support` will send TypeSafe: over it the run refuses, and says to narrow it with `--file` or to raise this key, so a runaway walk, such as a scanner that began reading a generated file, cannot spend without limit. Set at about three times the 437 the whole repository held on 2026-09-30 before this change's own files were added (`mise run citations:support --dry-run` counts it now), so ordinary growth never trips it. A run with no `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` sends nothing, judges offline by word overlap (`citationSupportOverlapMinShare`) and is not held to it. Raising it is a person's edit; lowering it below that count refuses every whole-repository run. Where it loses: a repository that grows past it refuses the whole-repository run until the key is raised, and `--file` still works.
citationSupportOverlapMinShareMeans: The offline fallback's threshold: when `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` is not set, `mise run citations:support` weighs each word by how few of the scanned files hold it, leaves out the pointer's own words and its section's heading, and prints a citation whose cited passage holds less than this share of its claim's weight; a share at or above it is silent. The maintainer chose this fallback on 2026-09-30 (`asdlc-openspec-6yt.6`) over Claude Code headless and the Anthropic API, knowing the loss below. Measured that day over the 442 citations the command judges, against one TypeSafe run on `jev-1.13.0` that put 27 under `citationSupportMinProbability` (0.3): the share ranks those 27 below the rest at an AUC of 0.69; at 0.05 it prints 8, 2 of them among the 27; at 0.1, 26 and 5; at 0.15, 57 and 10; at 0.2, 85 and 11; at 0.3, 156 and 15. It is 0.1 because that prints a list about as long as the TypeSafe one, which a person reads to the end. Raising it prints more citations, most of them sound; lowering it prints only the claims that share almost nothing with their section. Where it loses: the `bd` row of `docs/playbook.md` § 1. Words you will meet (line 53 that day), the one defect a reading confirmed among TypeSafe's list, cites `README.md` § Setup for a sentence that sits in that file's table, and its claim shares 0.33 of its weight with § Setup, so only a setting above 0.33 shows it, where 0.3 already prints 156. A claim that contradicts its section shares its words and is silent, and a claim that paraphrases its section is printed; the `--min` flag re-runs it at another share.
promptIncidentMinProbabilityMeans: The probability of yes at or above which `mise run prompts:incidents` (`scripts/prompt-incidents.mjs`) prints a paragraph of a prompt as telling an incident with no date, tracker id, pull request number or run id to mark it; under it a paragraph is silent. Set from the 2026-09-29 experiment in the notes of `asdlc-openspec-6yt.5`, over a sample of 60 paragraphs with `jev-1.13.0`: 40 real prompt paragraphs as they were, and 20 with an incident from the prompt-run analyses appended, 10 dated and 10 undated; at 0.5 it flagged all 20 and none of the 40, an AUC of 1.000. That experiment asked of one paragraph at a time, in its own wording and not this command's, and judged no workflow literal, so the figure is a starting point to re-measure on the real data, as the epic's note of 2026-09-30 asks of every sibling's threshold, and not a measurement of this command. Raising it prints fewer paragraphs and misses an incident told in passing; lowering it prints more rules that read like one. Where it loses: a rule worded as a worked example ("a session that pushes before it rebases ...") reads like an incident, and a person reads a false finding.
promptIncidentMinWordsMeans: The fewest words a paragraph of a prompt must hold for `mise run prompts:incidents` to ask TypeSafe whether it tells an incident; one with fewer is counted as not judged and sent nowhere. A paragraph is a run of non-blank lines of a markdown prompt, or of one string or template literal of a workflow, whose substitutions cut it. At 158b73e on 2026-10-05 the 32 prompts gave 2,655 paragraphs, 1,504 of them under four words and 1,480 of those in the four workflows, where `build-change-task.js` alone gave 858; each of the 96 distinct three-word paragraphs was a heading, a fragment of a message that a substitution cuts, or code, and none told an event (each counted over `promptLines` in `scripts/check-prompts.mjs`, by the session that set the key; no gate re-derives them). It is a choice, not a measurement: the experiment behind `promptIncidentMinProbability` judged whole markdown paragraphs and none this short. Raising it leaves out short sentences; lowering it sends the workflows' keys, type names and separators as questions, hundreds in one request. Where it loses: an incident told in three words or fewer, or cut by a template literal's substitutions into fragments that short, is never judged.
githubAppIdMeans: The id of the agents' GitHub App (`docs/decisions.md` § D-51), which `scripts/github-app-token.mjs` puts as the `iss` of the JSON Web Token it signs with the App's private key when it asks GitHub for an installation token for the dev container's `git` and `gh`. Recorded by asdlc-openspec-owva.2 on 2026-10-05, from the App's settings page. GitHub checks the token's signature against the public key of the App this names, so a wrong id, or another App's with this App's key, gets every token refused, and the helper prints GitHub's answer. Where it loses: a fork, or a maintainer with an App of their own, mints nothing until a pull request changes this.
githubAppBotLoginMeans: The login of the agents' GitHub App's bot account, which the dev container commits as: `scripts/github-app-token.mjs identity` prints it as `user.name`, and `.devcontainer/entrypoint.sh` sets that in the container's `~/.gitconfig` at start when no `user.email` is set. Read 2026-10-06 from `gh api /users/asdlc-agent-j%5Bbot%5D`, which gave type Bot (asdlc-openspec-irvc). A wrong login gives commits a name that is not the App's, while `githubAppBotUserId` still ties them to the account through the email. Where it loses: an App renamed on GitHub keeps committing under the old name until this is edited, and a container whose `~/.gitconfig` was set before the edit keeps it until a rebuild discards that file, since the entrypoint leaves an email already set.
githubAppBotUserIdMeans: The id of that bot account, not the App's id (`githubAppId`): `scripts/github-app-token.mjs identity` makes `user.email` from it as `<this>+<githubAppBotLogin>@users.noreply.github.com`, the form GitHub documents for an account's noreply address (docs.github.com, "Email addresses reference", read 2026-10-06). GitHub attributes a commit with that email to the bot account, through a rename too, since the id is in it. Read 2026-10-06 from `gh api /users/asdlc-agent-j%5Bbot%5D` (asdlc-openspec-irvc). Where it loses: a commit is not signed by it, so GitHub shows no Verified badge on the container's commits, which only a commit the App creates through the API gets.
githubAppInstallationIdMeans: The installation of that App on this repository, whose installation token `scripts/github-app-token.mjs` asks for at `/app/installations/<this>/access_tokens`. A token asked for with no body reaches every repository the installation covers: asdlc-openspec-owva.2 asked for this one alone, and on 2026-10-06 such a token, minted in the dev container, listed 8 of the maintainer's repositories, this one among them (`gh api /installation/repositories`). The helper therefore asks for `githubAppTokenRepository` alone. The maintainer narrowed the installation to this repository alone the same day, in its settings on GitHub. asdlc-openspec-t4cz's note of 2026-10-06 records that on their word, not from a command: every token the helper mints names this one repository, so `gh api /installation/repositories` lists it alone whether the installation covers 1 repository or 8, and only a token minted from the App's key with no body lists what the installation covers. Added 2026-10-07 (asdlc-openspec-t4cz). Recorded by asdlc-openspec-owva.2 on 2026-10-05, from the App's settings page. Where it loses: an App uninstalled and installed again gets a new id, and every token is refused until this is edited.
githubAppTokenRepositoryMeans: The one repository, by its bare name, that a token `scripts/github-app-token.mjs` mints may reach: it sends `{"repositories": [<this>]}` with each request, which GitHub documents as narrowing that one token to the repositories named, among those the installation covers (docs.github.com, "Create an installation access token for an app", read 2026-10-06). This repository, since the dev container's sessions work here and its tracker's Dolt remote is here too (`.beads/config.yaml`). Without it, every token reached the 8 repositories the installation covered on 2026-10-06 (`githubAppInstallationIdMeans`). Where it loses: it narrows the tokens the helper mints, and no other: a session can read the App's key, which the container mounts for it, and mint a token for every repository the installation covers. On the maintainer's word, the installation covers this repository alone since 2026-10-06 (`githubAppInstallationIdMeans`), so `githubAppTokenRepository` and the installation name the same repository. A repository later added to the installation on GitHub is open to such a token at once, and no gate reads the installation's list to see it. Added 2026-10-07 (asdlc-openspec-t4cz). Decided 2026-10-06 (asdlc-openspec-owva.4), from its adversarial review's finding, which a skeptic upheld.
githubAppRepositoryOwnerMeans: The account that owns `githubAppTokenRepository`, which the App is installed on. `.devcontainer/entrypoint.sh` clones `https://github.com/<this>/<githubAppTokenRepository>.git` into the container's workspace volume at its first start, with no token, since the repository is public (`gh repo view --json visibility`, 2026-10-06). It reads both keys from the copy of this record `.devcontainer/Dockerfile` puts in the image, because the clone that holds this file does not exist yet (docs/decisions.md § D-54). A changed value reaches a container only once it is rebuilt, and only one whose volume holds no clone yet. Where it loses: the high-risk floor holds it to a person through `githubApp*`, because a wrong value clones another account's code into every new container, where the entrypoint runs `npm ci` and its hooks. Recorded 2026-10-06 (asdlc-openspec-vvns), from `gh repo view --json nameWithOwner`.
githubAppTokenRefreshSecondsMeans: How many seconds of a kept installation token's life must be left for `scripts/github-app-token.mjs` to hand it out again; with fewer, it mints a fresh one and keeps that. GitHub's installation token lasts an hour (docs.github.com, "Generating an installation access token for a GitHub App", read 2026-10-06), and `git` and `gh` each read a token once, when a command starts, so a command must end before the token it read expires. 1800 gives every command at least half an hour, which holds a watcher run in the background, such as `gh pr checks --watch` while `verify` runs, and costs one call to GitHub each half hour a session works. Raising it toward 3600 mints more often, at 3599 once for every command; lowering it hands out a token a long command outlives. Where it loses: one `gh` or `git` command that runs longer than half an hour, started as its token's last half hour began, is refused midway, where a shorter-lived command, or a token minted afresh, would not be. Decided 2026-10-06 (asdlc-openspec-owva.4).
langfuseBaseUrlMeans: Where `scripts/prompt-run-figures.mjs` sends every request, and with it each project's public and secret key as basic auth: Langfuse Cloud's US region, where the maintainer chose on 2026-09-26 to trace the host's sessions (asdlc-openspec-pnp) and where asdlc-openspec-ic9h.12 creates the container's project. The script refuses a value that is not a URL's origin alone, and one that is not https, but for a loopback host, which only its selftest's stub uses. On the high-risk floor through `langfuse*` in `prReviewHighRiskJsonKeys`, since a changed host receives both projects' secret keys at the prompt review's next run. Where it loses: both projects must sit in one region; a project in another reads as refused keys (401) until this changes. Decided 2026-10-09 (asdlc-openspec-ic9h.4).
langfuseObservationsPathMeans: The path, on `langfuseBaseUrl`, of version 2 of Langfuse's observations API, which filters on a session id and a start-time window, returns only the field groups a request names, and pages by cursor (Langfuse's OpenAPI spec, https://cloud.langfuse.com/generated/api/openapi.yml, read 2026-10-09; asdlc-openspec-ic9h.10). Version 1, /api/public/observations, pages by number and returns every field, input and output among them, so a reader of it would hold every prompt and tool output in memory. A server without version 2 answers 404, which the script records as a failure naming this path, never as a run with no trace. The script refuses a path that opens with `//` or holds a backslash, which `new URL()` resolves to another host, past every check on `langfuseBaseUrl`, as the branch's adversarial review showed. Decided 2026-10-09 (asdlc-openspec-ic9h.4).
langfuseFieldGroupsMeans: The field groups each request asks for, joined by commas as `fields`. `core` and `basic` hold the type, name, level, times and session id the figures read, and `usage` holds `usageDetails` and `totalCost`. Without `fields`, Langfuse returns `core` and `basic` alone, with no token count, as the first read in asdlc-openspec-ic9h.10 showed. The script refuses a list without these three, and one naming a group that holds an observation's text, which its `TEXT_GROUPS` lists from Langfuse's spec; it also keeps no field it does not count. Adding `model` would fill the per-token prices, which are not costs. Decided 2026-10-09 (asdlc-openspec-ic9h.4).
langfusePageLimitMeans: How many observations one request asks for, as `limit`: Langfuse's largest, since the route's query schema refuses more (`lte(1000)`, web/src/features/public-api/types/observations.ts in langfuse/langfuse at eecc7d0, read 2026-10-09), where the default is 50. A larger page spends fewer of the organisation's requests, 30 a minute on the Hobby plan (https://langfuse.com/faq/all/api-limits.md, read 2026-10-09). The selftest sets it to 2, so that its control reads one run across four pages. Decided 2026-10-09 (asdlc-openspec-ic9h.4).

container.why: the dev container's sessions, which trace to a project of their own (docs/decisions/asdlc-openspec-ic9h.md, item 6; asdlc-openspec-ic9h.12)
container.offBecause: Langfuse's plugin holds back a turn that started background work and sends it whole in one upload, which Langfuse can lose without a sign, so a session's figures can hold a fraction of its work (asdlc-openspec-s5l3; asdlc-openspec-kqy2). Off until a release of the plugin fixes both defects asdlc-openspec-rdcw reports and one session's figures match its transcript.

host.why: the maintainer's own sessions on the host, traced since 2026-09-26 (asdlc-openspec-pnp)
host.offBecause: Langfuse's plugin holds back a turn that started background work and sends it whole in one upload, which Langfuse can lose without a sign, so a session's figures can hold a fraction of its work (asdlc-openspec-s5l3; asdlc-openspec-kqy2). The host runs the same plugin, and no host session's figures were compared with its transcript. Off until a release of the plugin fixes both defects asdlc-openspec-rdcw reports and one session's figures match its transcript.

langfuseProjectsMeans: Each Langfuse project `scripts/prompt-run-figures.mjs` reads, keyed by the name its output gives the project, with the environment variables that hold its public key and its secret key, and its reason. The prompt-review environment's secrets take these names (asdlc-openspec-ic9h.9). A project with both variables set is read, one with neither is reported as not configured, and one with only one set is a failure naming the other. A row may also give `offBecause`, a reason in text, which turns its project off: the script reports it as `not read: <reason>` and sends it no request, whatever its variables hold, and a person turns it back on by removing the field. Both rows have been turned off since 2026-10-10, at the maintainer's choice in asdlc-openspec-kqy2, because Langfuse's plugin can lose part of a session's trace without a sign (asdlc-openspec-s5l3). Where it loses: a session that started no background work sends its trace whole, and while its project is off the review gets none of its figures. The script runs nothing, and reads the pending analyses from a file `prompt-runs` wrote in a step that held none of these variables, so no code off the high-risk floor holds a key. Renaming a variable strands the secret under its old name, which then reads as not configured. On the high-risk floor through `langfuse*` in `prReviewHighRiskJsonKeys`. Decided 2026-10-09 (asdlc-openspec-ic9h.4).
langfuseTurnNameMeans: The name of the SPAN that Langfuse's Claude Code plugin opens for each turn, one user prompt and what follows it to the next (`open_turn_root_span` in hooks/langfuse_hook.py at v1.2.1, b5b7cc3, read 2026-10-09; the first read in asdlc-openspec-ic9h.10). `scripts/prompt-run-figures.mjs` counts these as a run's turns and sums their durations. A plugin release that renames it leaves every run at no turns, beside an `observations` count that shows the run was read. Decided 2026-10-09 (asdlc-openspec-ic9h.4).
langfuseToolNamePrefixMeans: What the plugin puts before a tool's name in the name of the TOOL observation it opens for each tool call: "Tool: Read" in the first read in asdlc-openspec-ic9h.10, and `f"Tool: {tool_name}"` in `emit_single_tool_observation` at v1.2.1, b5b7cc3. `scripts/prompt-run-figures.mjs` takes it off and counts the call under the name left, when that is an identifier its header gives the shape of, and under `(other)` when it is not or the prefix is missing, so no tool name carries text. A plugin release that changes it moves every call under `(other)`. Decided 2026-10-09 (asdlc-openspec-ic9h.4).
langfuseUsageBucketsMeans: Which keys of a GENERATION's `usageDetails` each token figure of `scripts/prompt-run-figures.mjs` sums. The keys are the ones the plugin writes from each assistant message's usage (`get_usage_details_from_row` and `get_cache_write_details` in hooks/langfuse_hook.py at v1.2.1, b5b7cc3): `input` and `output`, the cache read, and the cache write, as one key or split by its time to live, never both. Langfuse keeps each key as a bucket of its own (https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/features/token-and-cost-tracking.md, read 2026-10-09), so their sum counts no token twice. A key in no bucket but `langfuseUsageTotalKey` is summed under `unbucketed` and its name listed, so a change in the plugin or in Langfuse shows rather than skews a figure. Langfuse's own `inputUsage` sums every key whose name holds `input`, which would fold both caches into the input. asdlc-openspec-ic9h.10's second read, of 2026-10-10, showed `input`, `output`, `cache_read_input_tokens` and `input_cache_creation_1h` on the plugin's generations, and summed by these buckets they give the 74,543 input tokens and 230 output tokens asdlc-openspec-pnp's note recorded for that trace. Decided 2026-10-09 (asdlc-openspec-ic9h.4).
langfuseUsageTotalKeyMeans: The key Langfuse adds to a GENERATION's `usageDetails` as the sum of its other keys, which `scripts/prompt-run-figures.mjs` counts in no bucket, since counting it would count each token twice. Only what it holds past the other keys goes under `unbucketed`, listed by its name, so a total sent alone, as a client that reports one count sends it, still shows; a total below the other keys fails that run's read, since no figure could say which is right. asdlc-openspec-ic9h.10's second read, of 2026-10-10, showed it on both of a session's generations, at 38,597 = 8 + 97 + 36,033 + 2,459 and 36,176 = 10 + 133 + 13,856 + 22,177; the plugin writes no such key (`get_usage_details_from_row` in hooks/langfuse_hook.py at v1.2.1, b5b7cc3), so Langfuse adds it. The script refuses a policy with this key in a bucket of `langfuseUsageBuckets`. Where it loses: a usage type that Langfuse or the plugin one day names `total` for real tokens would be dropped unseen. Decided 2026-10-10 (asdlc-openspec-ic9h.4).
langfuseLookbackDaysMeans: How many days before its run id's time a run's window opens, when the run's session wrote no earlier analysis. The window ends at the run id's time, because a session works on after its analysis is written. It opens at the session's earlier analysis where there is one (`previous` in the pending section of `scripts/prompt-runs.mjs`). It is a choice, not a measurement. Where it loses: a session that ran for longer than this before its first analysis loses its earliest turns from the figures. And Langfuse moves the window's start up to its plan's data-access window, 30 days on Hobby, so a run older than that reads as no trace. Decided 2026-10-09 (asdlc-openspec-ic9h.4).
langfuseRetryLimitMeans: How many times `scripts/prompt-run-figures.mjs` sends one request again after a 429, each time after the seconds its Retry-After header gives, which Langfuse calls the authoritative wait (https://langfuse.com/faq/all/api-limits.md, read 2026-10-09); past it, the run's read fails as rate limited. The limit is the organisation's, shared by every key and project in it. It is a choice, not a measurement. Where it loses: a night when another client spends the organisation's minute fails the read, where a longer patience would have waited it out. Decided 2026-10-09 (asdlc-openspec-ic9h.4).
langfuseRetryMaxWaitSecondsMeans: The longest Retry-After `scripts/prompt-run-figures.mjs` waits out. A longer one fails the run's read as rate limited at once, so the workflow's step never sleeps for an hour on a header. Langfuse's limits are per minute (https://langfuse.com/faq/all/api-limits.md, read 2026-10-09). Decided 2026-10-09 (asdlc-openspec-ic9h.4).
langfuseRequestTimeoutSecondsMeans: The longest one request of `scripts/prompt-run-figures.mjs` may take before it is abandoned and the run's read fails as timed out. It is a choice, not a measurement: no page of `langfusePageLimit` rows has been timed. Where it loses: a slow night fails the read where a longer wait would have finished it, and the review reads that run as failed, not as missing. Decided 2026-10-09 (asdlc-openspec-ic9h.4).
